answer: Bounded-vouching trust graphs resist Sybil attacks by treating each agent as a vertex scored via max-flow from verified seeds across signed, quota-limited peer endorsements. Because cut capacity caps how far puppet subgraphs can ripple, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of consuming scarce endorsement slots per bridged identity, even at a zenith of internal self-linking. However, strict quotas hinder unconnected newcomers and weaken if adversaries compromise high-degree hubs.
